anzsic_codes.name: Toy, Sporting and Recreational Product Manufacturing

merger_description:
Platinum Equity, LLC (**Platinum Equity**), through a vehicle ultimately controlled by Platinum Equity, proposes to acquire all outstanding equity in SuperStroke International, LLC (**SuperStroke**) (the **Acquisition**). Existing unitholders in SuperStroke, including funds managed and advised by DAOL Private Equity Limited (**DAOL Private Equity**), will retain a roll-over interest in SuperStroke post-Acquisition.

Platinum Equity is a US-headquartered global private equity and investment strategies firm. The Platinum Equity group specialises in the merger, acquisition and operation of companies providing services and solutions to customers in a broad range of sectors including business services, information technology, telecommunication, logistics, metal services, manufacturing and distribution.

SuperStroke is a US-based manufacturer and supplier of golfing equipment components, with a focus on grips used for clubs and putters. SuperStroke supplies aftermarket replacement grips to consumers through distributors and online platforms and also supplies grips to golf equipment manufacturers.

DAOL Private Equity is a Seoul-based investment firm. Funds managed and advised by DAOL Private Equity control Technique Golf Holdings Co., Ltd, a special purpose vehicle that owns SuperStroke.

events.title: Notification waiver determination published

determination_table_content.details:
In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information provided in the application, the ACCC
considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material
lessening of competition given there is no horizontal overlap or
vertical relationship between Platinum Equity (and its connected
entities) and SuperStroke in the supply of golfing equipment in
Australia.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s guidance on notification
waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
